item.research_question: Can the thermodynamic principle of high entropy stabilization be applied to design self-regenerative supported transition metal catalysts that resist sintering through reversible exsolution-dissolution cycles?
item.material_system: Cubic high-entropy oxide Zr0.5(NiFeCuMnCo)0.5Ox (Zr:Ni:Fe:Cu:Mn:Co molar ratio 5:1:1:1:1:1) and comparative binary/ternary doped ZrO2 systems (e.g., Zr0.5Cu0.5Ox, Zr0.5(CuMn)0.5Ox)
item.processing_route: Mechanochemical synthesis: ZrCl4, NiCl2, FeCl3, CuCl2·2H2O, MnCl2, CoCl2·6H2O, and NaCl were ball-milled for 2 hours total; NaOH was added and milled for 1 hour; calcination in air at 550 °C for 3 hours (heating rate 2 K min−1); followed by washing with water and ethanol and drying at 70 °C
item.test_conditions: Redox cycling: H2 treatment at 600 °C for 2 h followed by Air treatment at 550 °C; Catalytic testing: CO2 hydrogenation (RWGS) at 400 °C for >500 h continuous operation; Feed gas H2:CO2 = 3:1 at atmospheric pressure
key_findings: The high entropy Zr0.5(NiFeCuMnCo)0.5Ox achieved a specific surface area of 84 m2 g−1 due to mild crystallization at 550 °C and mechanochemical particle breakage.
In situ reversible exsolution of CoFeCuNi alloy nanoparticles and reintegration into the ZrO2 matrix were observed over three redox cycles (H2 600 °C + Air 550 °C).
The configurational entropy contribution (TΔSconfig = T × 12.7 J mol−1 K−1) was predominant in the Gibbs free energy (ΔG), driving the stability of the host structure.
During CO2 hydrogenation at 400 °C, the catalyst maintained ~29% CO2 conversion and >90% CO selectivity for over 500 hours without sintering.
Binary doped Zr0.5Cu0.5Ox showed excessive particle growth (average size 37.7 nm) and severe deactivation within 40 hours, unlike the high entropy variant.
Impregnated 5% and 10% NiFeCuCo/ZrOx catalysts suffered severe deactivation within 1–3 hours, whereas the high entropy oxide lasted >500 hours.
XPS analysis confirmed the formation of metallic Co0, Ni0, Cu0, and Fe0 species during H2 reduction, while Mn remained largely as MnO.
item.mechanism: The high configurational entropy lowers the Gibbs free energy of the solid solution, stabilizing the host matrix against sintering. During reduction, transition metals exsolve to form active alloy nanoparticles; during oxidation, the entropy-added motivation drives the reintegration of these metals back into the parent oxide lattice, creating a self-regenerative cycle that confines metal species and prevents agglomeration.
item.limitations: The study notes that binary and ternary doped ZrO2 samples formed impure phases or showed excessive particle growth, indicating that the high entropy effect is critical for the observed stability; the authors also mention that the exsolved CoFeCuNi NPs could not be described as high entropy alloys themselves.
item.future_work: The authors propose that the current theory may inspire the design of more supported transition metal catalysts (STMCs) with excellent sintering-resistance performance and suggest that considering entropic contributions is just the beginning for developing unique materials for heterogeneous catalysis.
quotes: entropy driving force could promote the self-regeneration process is proposed
in situ reversible exsolution-dissolution of supported metallic species are observed in multi redox cycles
entropy-added motivation may drive the reintegration of CoFeCuNi alloy NPs into the parent ZrO2 matrix in air
